primaryFindings.explanation: The loop condition was changed from `i < values.length` to `i <= values.length`, causing the loop to attempt to access `values[values.length]`, which is out of bounds and will throw an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for any non-empty array.

decisions.reason: The patch explicitly changes the loop condition from `i < values.length` to `i <= values.length`. In Java, array indices range from `0` to `length - 1`. Accessing index `values.length` is always out of bounds. This causes an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for any non-empty array (and even for empty arrays if the loop body executes once with `i=0` and `length=0`, though technically `0 <= 0` is true, so it tries `values[0]` which fails). The severity is HIGH because it causes a repeatable crash (exception) on normal operation with valid input data.
